summary.title: Falsehoods Programmers Believe About Falsehoods Lists
summary.one_liner: A tongue-in-cheek list of meta falsehoods, i.e. common misconceptions programmers hold about "falsehoods programmers believe" lists themselves.
takeaways: Falsehood lists are a satirical genre cataloguing widely held programmer misconceptions.
The page applies that genre to itself, listing misconceptions about falsehood lists (e.g. that they are for programmers only, or that they make you an expert).
Some items are self-referential paradoxes, such as 'This list of falsehoods doesn't apply to itself.'
It is a companion to the author's curated 'Awesome Falsehoods Programmers Believe' list.
summary.summary: The page is a humorous meta list of falsehoods: statements programmers wrongly assume about falsehood lists, grouped under headings such as Falsehoods, List format, Implementation, Audience, and Meta. It was inspired by a Hacker News comment and is meant to complement the author's curated Awesome Falsehoods Programmers Believe list. A short archived Disqus comment adds further self-referential remarks. The content is a list of jokes rather than a technical tutorial.
